words.enDefinition: to tell a particular person that you are sorry for something you did

examples.en: I had to apologize to someone I had interrupted during our first committee meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次委员会会议上我打断了一个人，后来得「向那个人道歉」。

examples.en: How do you apologize to someone when you realise you called them by the wrong name?
examples.zh: 发现叫错了别人的名字时，你该怎么「向对方道歉」？

collocations: apologize to someone in person
apologize to someone privately
apologize to someone directly

words.enDefinition: to deliver a formal apology, often on behalf of an organisation or publicly

examples.en: The society chose to issue an apology after leaving two volunteers off the programme.
examples.zh: 节目单漏了两名志愿者的名字，社团决定「发表正式道歉」。

examples.en: The department agreed to issue an apology when it discovered the notice had misled students.
examples.zh: 系里发现通知误导了学生，同意「发表正式道歉」。

collocations: issue an apology promptly
issue an apology to those affected
decide to issue an apology

words.enDefinition: an apology made openly so people beyond those directly involved can hear or read it

examples.en: The club posted a public apology after the photograph was shared without everyone's consent.
examples.zh: 社团在没有征得所有人同意的情况下分享了照片，后来贴出「公开道歉」。

examples.en: I read the public apology in the student paper before attending the committee meeting.
examples.zh: 参加委员会会议前，我在学生报纸上读到了「公开道歉」。

collocations: issue a public apology
publish a public apology
call for a public apology

words.enDefinition: an apology communicated directly to the people involved without making it public

examples.en: I received a private apology after the tutor realised she had confused our two projects.
examples.zh: 导师发现把我们的两个项目弄混了，便向我「私下道歉」。

examples.en: We thought a private apology would give our teammate room to say how he felt.
examples.zh: 我们觉得「私下道歉」可以给队友留出空间，让他说说自己的感受。

collocations: offer a private apology
receive a private apology
accept a private apology

words.enDefinition: an apology that expresses genuine regret and is meant honestly

examples.en: He offered a sincere apology after leaving his partner to finish the whole presentation alone.
examples.zh: 他把整份演示丢给搭档一个人做完，后来向搭档作了「真诚的道歉」。

examples.en: I could tell it was a sincere apology when she asked what would help next.
examples.zh: 她问接下来自己能做什么，我听得出那是「真诚的道歉」。

collocations: offer a sincere apology
accept a sincere apology
deserve a sincere apology

words.enDefinition: an apology with no qualifications, reservations or excuses attached

examples.en: The editor made an unreserved apology for naming the wrong person in the campus article.
examples.zh: 校园报道写错了人名，编辑作了「毫无保留的道歉」。

examples.en: Her unreserved apology did more to ease the tension than the committee's original statement.
examples.zh: 和委员会最初的声明相比，她「毫无保留的道歉」更能缓解紧张气氛。

collocations: make an unreserved apology
offer an unreserved apology
issue an unreserved apology

words.enDefinition: an apology offered later than expected or after a long delay

examples.en: His belated apology arrived two weeks after the group had finished working together on the report.
examples.zh: 我们小组合作完成报告两周后，才收到他「迟来的道歉」。

examples.en: I appreciated the belated apology, although it came months after the comments in class.
examples.zh: 虽然那些课堂评论已经过去几个月，我还是感谢这份「迟来的道歉」。

collocations: offer a belated apology
receive a belated apology
a belated apology for the remark

words.enDefinition: an apology made with little effort, conviction or genuine feeling

examples.en: The team's half-hearted apology made it sound as if nobody wanted to discuss what happened.
examples.zh: 团队「敷衍的道歉」听起来像是谁都不想谈到底发生了什么。

examples.en: I could tell from his half-hearted apology that he wanted to leave the room quickly.
examples.zh: 从他那「敷衍的道歉」里，我听得出他想赶快离开房间。

collocations: give a half-hearted apology
accept a half-hearted apology
sound like a half-hearted apology

words.enDefinition: a statement of apology that depends on whether an event happened or someone was harmed

examples.en: The mediator asked how a conditional apology could leave the other person feeling unheard.
examples.zh: 调解员问，「附带条件的道歉」为什么会让对方觉得自己的感受没被听见。

examples.en: The editor's conditional apology left open whether the article had caused any actual harm.
examples.zh: 编辑「附带条件的道歉」没有说清那篇报道是否真的造成了伤害。

collocations: give a conditional apology
phrase something as a conditional apology
a conditional apology beginning with if

words.enDefinition: a statement presented as an apology that fails to express regret or recognise wrongdoing

examples.en: Several students called the statement a non-apology because it ignored the mistake entirely.
examples.zh: 几名学生说，那份声明是「没有实际道歉的说法」，因为根本没提到过错。

examples.en: His non-apology left the volunteers feeling that their concerns still had not been addressed.
examples.zh: 他那番「没有实际道歉的说法」让志愿者觉得，他们担心的问题仍未得到回应。

collocations: dismiss something as a non-apology
issue a non-apology
a carefully worded non-apology

words.enDefinition: a short written message expressing regret for something you did

examples.en: I left an apology note after forgetting to put the shared scissors back that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午我忘了把共用剪刀放回去，留了条「简短的道歉留言」。

examples.en: My roommate found the apology note beside the mug I had chipped the night before.
examples.zh: 室友在我前一晚碰掉一角的杯子旁找到了那条「简短的道歉留言」。

collocations: write an apology note
leave an apology note
receive an apology note

words.enDefinition: to signal that you recognise and are willing to receive someone's expression of regret

examples.en: You can accept an apology and still ask for time before working together again.
examples.zh: 你可以「接受道歉」，同时表示重新一起做事之前需要一段时间。

examples.en: I found it easier to accept an apology once we had discussed what happened openly.
examples.zh: 我们坦诚谈过事情的经过之后，我觉得更容易「接受道歉」。

collocations: choose to accept an apology
be ready to accept an apology
graciously accept an apology

words.enDefinition: to say or show that you do not consider a person's apology acceptable

examples.en: The club chose to reject an apology that failed to address the damaged equipment.
examples.zh: 那份道歉对器材损坏只字未提，社团决定「拒绝接受道歉」。

examples.en: I did not want to reject an apology before hearing what he planned to change.
examples.zh: 听完他打算怎么改之前，我不想「拒绝接受道歉」。

collocations: choose to reject an apology
publicly reject an apology
decide whether to reject an apology

words.enDefinition: to need to apologise to someone because of something you have done

examples.en: You owe someone an apology if you blame them for a decision they never made.
examples.zh: 如果你把别人没做的决定怪到对方头上，就「欠那个人一个道歉」。

examples.en: It's easy to know you owe someone an apology and still put it off.
examples.zh: 知道自己「欠某人一个道歉」，却还是一拖再拖，这种事并不少见。

collocations: realise you owe someone an apology
admit you owe someone an apology
feel you owe someone an apology

words.enDefinition: to tell someone that you would like them to apologise for what happened

examples.en: I decided to ask for an apology after a joke misrepresented what I had said.
examples.zh: 有人开玩笑时曲解了我的话，我决定「要求对方道歉」。

examples.en: The chair explained that students may ask for an apology without making a formal complaint.
examples.zh: 主席解释，学生可以「要求对方道歉」，无需提出正式投诉。

collocations: decide to ask for an apology
ask for an apology in private
ask for an apology from the organiser

words.enDefinition: it is appropriate or necessary for someone to apologise

examples.en: I think an apology is in order after we left your name off the poster.
examples.zh: 海报漏印了你的名字，我觉得「应该道个歉」。

examples.en: The committee agreed that an apology is in order for the way volunteers were treated.
examples.zh: 委员会认为，那样对待志愿者，「应该道个歉」。

collocations: an apology is in order for the delay
perhaps an apology is in order
an apology is in order here

words.enDefinition: a polite, often formal way of asking someone to accept that you are sorry

examples.en: Please accept my apologies for sending the room number before I had checked the booking.
examples.zh: 我没核对预约就发了房间号，「请接受我的歉意」。

examples.en: Please accept my apologies for the delay in replacing the equipment we borrowed last month.
examples.zh: 我们上个月借的器材迟迟没有换好，「请接受我的歉意」。

collocations: please accept my apologies for the delay
please accept my apologies for the error
please accept my apologies for any inconvenience

words.enDefinition: a brief polite expression of regret, often used in a professional exchange

examples.en: My apologies for sending the invitation to the wrong group yesterday afternoon.
examples.zh: 「抱歉」，昨天下午我把邀请发错了群。

examples.en: My apologies. I misread the time and arrived after the demonstration had already finished.
examples.zh: 「抱歉」。我看错了时间，到的时候演示已经结束了。

collocations: my apologies for the oversight
my apologies for the delay
my apologies for the confusion

words.enDefinition: a polite expression of regret for causing someone difficulty or extra effort

examples.en: Sorry for the inconvenience, but we need to move tomorrow's meeting to the smaller room.
examples.zh: 「给大家添麻烦了，抱歉」，但明天的会议得移到那个较小的房间。

examples.en: The note said sorry for the inconvenience and gave directions to another printer nearby.
examples.zh: 通知上写着「给大家添麻烦了，抱歉」，还指了去附近另一台打印机的路。

collocations: say sorry for the inconvenience
write sorry for the inconvenience
sorry for the inconvenience this caused

words.enDefinition: a friendly apology for a mistake involving confusion about people, arrangements or details

examples.en: Sorry for the mix-up. I wrote the rehearsal time in the wrong column of the schedule.
examples.zh: 「把事情弄混了，抱歉」。我在日程表上写错了排练时间那一栏。

examples.en: Sorry for the mix-up with your handout. I will bring the right one.
examples.zh: 「给你的讲义弄混了，抱歉」。我会把对的那份带过来。

collocations: sorry for the mix-up with your booking
sorry for the mix-up earlier
really sorry for the mix-up

words.enDefinition: a polite apology to someone who has been waiting because of you

examples.en: Sorry to keep you waiting, the previous group needed another minute to clear the room.
examples.zh: 「抱歉让你久等了」，前一组需要再花一点时间收拾完房间。

examples.en: Sorry to keep you waiting, I had to find the key for the rehearsal space.
examples.zh: 「抱歉让你久等了」，我刚才得去找排练室的钥匙。

collocations: say sorry to keep you waiting
sorry to keep you waiting outside
sorry to keep you waiting so long

words.enDefinition: a direct apology offered immediately after arriving later than agreed

examples.en: Sorry I'm late, I went to the wrong entrance and had to walk around.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我迟到了」，我走错了入口，只好绕了一圈。

examples.en: Sorry I'm late, the seminar ran over and I did not want to interrupt.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我迟到了」，研讨课拖堂了，我不想打断他们。

collocations: say sorry I'm late
sorry I'm late to the meeting
sorry I'm late again

words.enDefinition: an apology for failing to give someone the help or support they were counting on

examples.en: Sorry I let you down when I forgot to bring the materials for your presentation.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我让你失望了」，我忘了给你带演示要用的材料。

examples.en: Sorry I let you down, I should have told you sooner that I couldn't come.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我让你失望了」，我应该早一点告诉你我来不了。

collocations: say sorry I let you down
I'm sorry I let you down
sorry I let you down yesterday

words.enDefinition: an apology for something you did that hurt another person's feelings

examples.en: I'm sorry I hurt you when I dismissed your suggestion in front of the group.
examples.zh: 我当着小组的面没把你的建议当回事，「抱歉我伤害了你」。

examples.en: I'm sorry I hurt you, and I'll listen if you want to tell me more.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我伤害了你」，如果你愿意多说一点，我会听。

collocations: say I'm sorry I hurt you
I'm sorry I hurt you with that joke
I'm sorry I hurt you yesterday

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that you regret a remark and believe it was wrong to make it

examples.en: I shouldn't have said that about your draft before hearing why you wrote it that way.
examples.zh: 在听你解释为什么那样写之前，「我不该那样说你的稿子」。

examples.en: I shouldn't have said that, especially in front of everyone else in the study group.
examples.zh: 「那话我不该说」，尤其不该当着学习小组所有人的面说。

collocations: say I shouldn't have said that
admit I shouldn't have said that
I shouldn't have said that in public

words.expression: I didn't mean to hurt you
words.lemma: i didn't mean to hurt you
words.enDefinition: explains that you did not intend to upset or cause pain to the other person
acceptedEnVariants: I didn't mean to hurt you

examples.en: I didn't mean to hurt you when I made that joke about your presentation.
examples.zh: 我拿你的演示开那个玩笑时，「没想伤害你」。

examples.en: I didn't mean to hurt you, but I understand why the message upset you.
examples.zh: 「我没想伤害你」，但我明白那条消息为什么让你难受。

collocations: explain I didn't mean to hurt you
I didn't mean to hurt you with that comment
I didn't mean to hurt you at all

words.expression: I didn't mean to sound dismissive
words.lemma: i didn't mean to sound dismissive
words.zhGloss: 我没想用轻慢的语气说话
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that one's words may have sounded as though the other person's concerns were unimportant
acceptedZhAnswers: 我没想用轻慢的语气说话
acceptedEnVariants: I didn't mean to sound dismissive

examples.en: I didn't mean to sound dismissive when you raised the issue in the group meeting.
examples.zh: 你在小组会议上提出问题时，「我没想用轻慢的语气说话」。

examples.en: I didn't mean to sound dismissive, but I understand why my reply came across that way.
examples.zh: 「我没想用轻慢的语气说话」，但我理解你为什么觉得我的回答很敷衍。

collocations: I didn't mean to sound dismissive of your idea
I didn't mean to sound dismissive in my reply
I didn't mean to sound dismissive when I said that

words.enDefinition: admits that you acted before considering the consequences or details fully

examples.en: I didn't think it through before offering our reserved room to another group that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午把我们预约的房间让给另一个小组前，「我没有想周全」。

examples.en: I didn't think it through, and I should have checked whether everyone could stay later.
examples.zh: 「我没有想周全」，应该先问问大家能不能多待一会儿。

collocations: admit I didn't think it through
say I didn't think it through
I didn't think it through before deciding

words.expression: I could have handled that better
words.lemma: i could have handled that better
words.zhGloss: 我当时可以处理得更好
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that there was a better way to deal with a situation
acceptedZhAnswers: 我当时可以处理得更好
acceptedEnVariants: I could have handled that better

examples.en: I could have handled that better when we disagreed about who should lead the meeting.
examples.zh: 我们对谁主持会议意见不同时，「我当时可以处理得更好」。

examples.en: I could have handled that better, especially when I saw you were being left out.
examples.zh: 「我当时可以处理得更好」，尤其在我已经看出你被排除在外时。

collocations: admit I could have handled that better
realise I could have handled that better
I could have handled that better in person

words.enDefinition: admits that your experience or knowledge should have stopped you from doing something unwise

examples.en: I should have known better than to promise a room before I had booked it.
examples.zh: 房间还没订下来就向大家保证有房间，「我本该知道那样不妥」。

examples.en: I should have known better than to assume the new students had seen the announcement.
examples.zh: 我以为新同学都看过通知，「我本该知道那样不妥」。

collocations: admit I should have known better
I should have known better than to rush
I should have known better than to assume

words.enDefinition: admits that you should have checked a detail before acting or telling someone

examples.en: I should have checked first, as the studio was already booked for the afternoon.
examples.zh: 工作室下午已经有人订了，「我应该先核实一下」。

examples.en: I should have checked first instead of sending everyone to the building we used last week.
examples.zh: 「我应该先核实一下」，而不是让大家都去上周用的那栋楼。

collocations: admit I should have checked first
I should have checked first with the tutor
I should have checked first with you

words.expression: I should have told you sooner
words.lemma: i should have told you sooner
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that an important thing should have been communicated earlier
acceptedEnVariants: I should have told you sooner

examples.en: I should have told you sooner that the microphone was no longer available for rehearsal.
examples.zh: 麦克风已经没法用来排练了，「我应该早点告诉你」。

examples.en: I should have told you sooner, so you could have made another arrangement for Friday.
examples.zh: 「我应该早点告诉你」，这样你本来可以为周五另作安排。

collocations: admit I should have told you sooner
I should have told you sooner about the change
I should have told you sooner that I couldn't come

words.enDefinition: says plainly that the speaker wishes they had not made a remark

examples.en: I regret what I said before I had heard your side of the story.
examples.zh: 在听你讲事情经过之前我就说了那番话，「现在我很后悔」。

examples.en: I regret what I said to the volunteers during yesterday's long rehearsal for the event.
examples.zh: 「我后悔说了那番话」，就是昨天排练时我对志愿者说的那些话。

collocations: acknowledge I regret what I said
say I regret what I said
I regret what I said about your work

words.enDefinition: expresses strong regret or distress about something that has happened

examples.en: I realised how much extra work I caused, and I feel awful about it.
examples.zh: 我意识到给你添了多少工作，「为这事感到很难受」。

examples.en: I feel awful about it because you counted on me to organise the room booking.
examples.zh: 你指望我负责预订房间，所以「我为这事感到很难受」。

collocations: I still feel awful about it
I feel awful about it now
I feel awful about it because you trusted me

words.zhGloss: 我为刚才的事感到难为情
words.enDefinition: expresses discomfort or shame about an incident, often involving one's own behaviour
acceptedZhAnswers: 我为刚才的事感到难为情

examples.en: I'm embarrassed about what happened when I walked into the wrong workshop and interrupted the speaker.
examples.zh: 我走错了工作坊，还打断了发言的人，「这事让我很难为情」。

examples.en: I'm embarrassed about what happened in front of everyone at yesterday's society meeting.
examples.zh: 昨天在社团会议上当着大伙儿发生的事，「让我很难为情」。

collocations: admit I'm embarrassed about what happened
say I'm embarrassed about what happened
I'm embarrassed about what happened yesterday

words.expression: I'm not proud of how I acted
words.lemma: i'm not proud of how i acted
words.zhGloss: 我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that the way one behaved did not meet one's own standards
acceptedZhAnswers: 我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not proud of how I acted

examples.en: I'm not proud of how I acted when we disagreed about the rehearsal space.
examples.zh: 我们对排练场地有分歧时，「我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧」。

examples.en: I'm not proud of how I acted, and I want to hear your side now.
examples.zh: 「我为自己当时的做法感到惭愧」，现在想听听你的看法。

collocations: acknowledge I'm not proud of how I acted
say I'm not proud of how I acted
I'm not proud of how I acted yesterday

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that your treatment of another person was unjust or unreasonable

examples.en: It was unfair of me to blame you for a decision the committee made together.
examples.zh: 决定是委员会一起做的，我却怪你，「那样做对你不公平」。

examples.en: It was unfair of me to expect you to stay late without asking you first.
examples.zh: 没先问你就指望你多留一会儿，「那样做对你不公平」。

collocations: it was unfair of me to assume
it was unfair of me to say that
admit it was unfair of me

words.enDefinition: states that you accept all responsibility for a mistake or outcome

examples.en: I take full responsibility for sending the incorrect schedule to the volunteers on Monday.
examples.zh: 「我承担全部责任」，周一是我把错误的时间表发给了志愿者。

examples.en: I take full responsibility, and I've already arranged a replacement session for the students affected.
examples.zh: 「我承担全部责任」，而且已给受影响的同学安排了补上的场次。

collocations: I take full responsibility for the mistake
I take full responsibility for what happened
say I take full responsibility

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge that a mistake was yours and accept the duty to address it

examples.en: I decided to take ownership of the mistake and contact the affected classmates myself.
examples.zh: 我决定「主动承担过错并处理」，自己联系受影响的同学。

examples.en: Our supervisor urged us to take ownership of the mistake instead of ignoring the feedback.
examples.zh: 主管劝我们「主动承担过错并处理」，别把意见放在一边不管。

collocations: choose to take ownership of the mistake
be willing to take ownership of the mistake
take ownership of the mistake early

words.enDefinition: to admit that you have done something wrong, especially after keeping quiet about it

examples.en: I decided to own up when our tutor asked who had deleted the shared table.
examples.zh: 导师问是谁删了共享表格，我决定「坦白承认过错」。

examples.en: The team agreed it was better to own up than let someone else be blamed.
examples.zh: 队友们认为，最好「坦白承认过错」，免得其他人背锅。

collocations: own up to a mistake
own up to what you did
decide to own up

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge that something went wrong because of one's actions or omissions

examples.en: The organiser chose to admit fault after realising she had sent two conflicting dates.
examples.zh: 组织者发现自己发了两个互相矛盾的日期，决定「承认有过错」。

examples.en: I was ready to admit fault once we checked the records from both meetings.
examples.zh: 我们核对两次会议的记录后，我愿意「承认有过错」。

collocations: willing to admit fault
refuse to admit fault
choose to admit fault

words.enDefinition: to openly recognise the effect that an action or decision had on other people

examples.en: The editor wanted to acknowledge the impact of the error on the students named.
examples.zh: 编辑想「承认造成的影响」，也就是那处错误怎样波及了被点名的学生。

examples.en: Before explaining my reasons, I tried to acknowledge the impact on the rest of the group.
examples.zh: 解释原因之前，我先试着「承认造成的影响」，包括给其他组员添的麻烦。

collocations: acknowledge the impact on others
fail to acknowledge the impact
openly acknowledge the impact

words.enDefinition: to recognise openly that someone acted wrongly, especially in an official or serious situation

examples.en: The committee voted to acknowledge wrongdoing in its response to the former volunteers that week.
examples.zh: 委员会投票决定，在当周给前志愿者的回应中「承认行为不当」。

examples.en: I thought the statement should acknowledge wrongdoing before it explained the new event rules.
examples.zh: 我认为那份声明应该先「承认行为不当」，再解释新活动规则。

collocations: publicly acknowledge wrongdoing
refuse to acknowledge wrongdoing
fail to acknowledge wrongdoing

words.enDefinition: to accept being held responsible for something that went wrong, even if others were involved

examples.en: I did not expect my teammate to take the blame for the group's missed deadline.
examples.zh: 我没想到队友会为整个小组错过截止日期「承担过错的责任」。

examples.en: She agreed to take the blame because she had approved the final draft herself.
examples.zh: 她同意「承担过错的责任」，因为最终稿是她亲自批准的。

collocations: take the blame for an error
be willing to take the blame
let someone else take the blame

words.enDefinition: responsible for an error, problem or harmful result

examples.en: We looked at both messages before deciding who was at fault for the confusion.
examples.zh: 我们查看了两条消息，才判断谁对这场混乱「负有过错」。

examples.en: I knew I was at fault when I saw the outdated timetable in my email.
examples.zh: 看到邮件里那份过时的时间表，我知道自己「负有过错」。

collocations: be partly at fault
find someone at fault
decide who is at fault

words.enDefinition: informally accepts personal responsibility for an error or problem

examples.en: I forgot to send the final rehearsal times, so that's on me, not you.
examples.zh: 我忘了发最终排练时间，「这件事怪我」，跟你没关系。

examples.en: That's on me. I should have checked the cupboard before saying the equipment was there.
examples.zh: 「这件事怪我」。我应该先看一眼柜子，再说器材在里面。

collocations: say that's on me
that's on me entirely
that's on me for forgetting

words.enDefinition: to admit the truth about something that you had been keeping secret

examples.en: I decided to come clean about why the volunteer certificates had not been printed yet.
examples.zh: 我决定「把隐瞒的实情说出来」，解释志愿者证书为什么还没印。

examples.en: Our talk made it easier for me to come clean about deleting the original schedule.
examples.zh: 谈过之后，我比较能「把隐瞒的实情说出来」，承认是我删了原时间表。

collocations: come clean about a mistake
decide to come clean
come clean to someone

words.enDefinition: to show or say that you think someone is to blame for a problem

examples.en: I did not want to point the finger until we knew why the booking disappeared.
examples.zh: 在弄清预约为什么不见了之前，我不想「指责任何人」。

examples.en: It is easy to point the finger at one person when a group project fails.
examples.zh: 小组项目失败时，很容易就「指责某个人」。

collocations: point the finger at someone
refuse to point the finger
quick to point the finger

words.enDefinition: to make somebody else appear responsible for something you or another person did

examples.en: The volunteers felt the organiser was trying to shift the blame onto the venue staff.
examples.zh: 志愿者觉得，组织者试图「把责任推给」场地工作人员。

examples.en: I wanted to explain the timeline without trying to shift the blame for the delay.
examples.zh: 我想把时间经过解释清楚，同时承担延误的责任，不把它「推给别人」。

collocations: shift the blame onto someone else
attempt to shift the blame
refuse to shift the blame

words.enDefinition: to make sure you answer for your actions and follow through on commitments

examples.en: It helps to hold yourself accountable by setting a date to check your progress.
examples.zh: 定一个日期来查看进展，有助于「要求自己承担责任」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how you hold yourself accountable when a project depends on your part.
examples.zh: 导师问，一个项目离不开你负责的部分时，你怎样「要求自己承担责任」。

collocations: hold yourself accountable for your actions
learn to hold yourself accountable
ways to hold yourself accountable

words.enDefinition: considering what happened with knowledge that was not available at the time

examples.en: In hindsight, I should have asked why the group preferred the original plan for the event.
examples.zh: 「事后回看」，我本该问问小组为什么更喜欢原来的活动计划。

examples.en: It was a poor decision in hindsight, but we had only a minute to choose.
examples.zh: 「事后回看」，这个决定不妥，但当时我们只有一分钟来选。

collocations: seem obvious in hindsight
in hindsight it makes sense
recognise something in hindsight

words.enDefinition: an error made without intending to deceive or harm anyone

examples.en: It was an honest mistake, but I still needed to correct the sign-up list.
examples.zh: 虽然是「无心之失」，我还是得把报名名单纠正过来。

examples.en: She called it an honest mistake after seeing the two event names looked similar.
examples.zh: 她发现两个活动名字很像，就说那是「无心之失」。

collocations: make an honest mistake
recognise an honest mistake
explain that it was an honest mistake

words.enDefinition: a polite way to acknowledge that you failed to notice or do something

examples.en: It was an oversight on my part to leave the last volunteer off the list.
examples.zh: 我漏掉了最后一位志愿者的名字，「是我疏忽了」。

examples.en: That was an oversight on my part, and I'll send you the corrected timetable today.
examples.zh: 「是我疏忽了」，今天我会把改好的时间表发给你。

collocations: it was an oversight on my part
acknowledge that it was an oversight on my part
explain that it was an oversight on my part

words.enDefinition: informally explains that you forgot something you had intended to do or remember

examples.en: I meant to return the key yesterday, but it slipped my mind after class.
examples.zh: 我本来打算昨天还钥匙，可一下课「我一时忘了」。

examples.en: It slipped my mind that I'd promised to bring the markers for our poster session.
examples.zh: 「我一时忘了」答应过要带海报展示用的记号笔。

collocations: admit it slipped my mind
it completely slipped my mind
it slipped my mind after class

words.enDefinition: a brief failure to think clearly or make a sound decision

examples.en: I called it a lapse in judgment after realising I had repeated a rumour.
examples.zh: 我发现自己转述了传言，承认那是「一时判断失误」。

examples.en: The chair said a lapse in judgment had led her to share the draft too early.
examples.zh: 主席说，自己「一时判断失误」，把草稿发得太早了。

collocations: admit a lapse in judgment
apologise for a lapse in judgment
a brief lapse in judgment

words.enDefinition: a remark made without considering how it might affect another person

examples.en: I apologised for the thoughtless comment I made as we left the studio together.
examples.zh: 我们一起离开展示室时，我道歉了，为的是之前那句「欠考虑的评论」。

examples.en: One thoughtless comment changed the mood of the discussion just before the break.
examples.zh: 休息前一句「欠考虑的评论」改变了讨论的气氛。

collocations: make a thoughtless comment
apologise for a thoughtless comment
regret a thoughtless comment

words.enDefinition: to upset another person emotionally through something you say or do

examples.en: It is easy to hurt someone's feelings when you joke about their work in public.
examples.zh: 公开拿别人的作品开玩笑，很容易「伤害那个人的感情」。

examples.en: I worried my remark could hurt someone's feelings even if it had sounded harmless to me.
examples.zh: 即使这话听来没什么，我也担心它会「伤害某人的感情」。

collocations: accidentally hurt someone's feelings
not mean to hurt someone's feelings
worry about hurting someone's feelings

words.enDefinition: to make people feel insulted, disrespected or upset

examples.en: I did not expect that remark to cause offence during such an informal conversation.
examples.zh: 我没想到那句话在这么随意的聊天中也会「冒犯别人」。

examples.en: The editor removed a joke that might cause offence to some readers of the paper.
examples.zh: 编辑删掉了一个可能「冒犯部分读者」的玩笑。

collocations: cause offence to someone
not intend to cause offence
words that may cause offence

words.enDefinition: to react as if you are being attacked when someone criticises or questions what you did

examples.en: I tend to get defensive when someone points out a mistake in front of everyone.
examples.zh: 有人当着大家的面指出错误时，我很容易「急于为自己辩解」。

examples.en: I tried not to get defensive when my partner explained why the decision hurt her.
examples.zh: 搭档解释那个决定为什么让她难过时，我尽量不「急于为自己辩解」。

collocations: try not to get defensive
get defensive about criticism
tend to get defensive

words.enDefinition: to speak to someone sharply and angrily, often in a brief reaction

examples.en: I sometimes snap at someone when I am rushed, and then regret how I sounded.
examples.zh: 着急的时候我有时会「突然冲别人发火」，过后又后悔自己语气不好。

examples.en: I know it is unfair to snap at someone for asking a perfectly reasonable question.
examples.zh: 我知道别人问了个完全合理的问题，我却「突然冲人家发火」，这不公平。

collocations: snap at someone for no good reason
snap at someone in a hurry
apologise for snapping at someone

words.enDefinition: to react angrily toward someone through strong criticism, harsh words or physical action

examples.en: I watched him lash out at someone who had only offered help with the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我看到他「猛地冲别人发泄怒气」，而那人只是主动说可以帮忙排练。

examples.en: When I feel cornered, I try to pause before I lash out at someone.
examples.zh: 觉得被逼到没退路时，我会先停一下，免得「猛地冲别人发泄怒气」。

collocations: lash out at someone in frustration
want to lash out at someone
verbally lash out at someone

words.enDefinition: to become angry suddenly and stop speaking or behaving calmly

examples.en: It is easy to lose your temper when the same equipment keeps going missing.
examples.zh: 同一件器材总是不见，很容易让人「发脾气」。

examples.en: I knew you were frustrated, but I did not expect you to lose your temper.
examples.zh: 我知道你很烦，但没想到你会「发脾气」。

collocations: lose your temper with someone
try not to lose your temper
be quick to lose your temper

words.enDefinition: to direct your anger at someone who did not cause the original problem

examples.en: When you have a rough day, try not to take it out on someone at home.
examples.zh: 一天过得不顺时，尽量别回家「拿别人出气」。

examples.en: I said it wasn't fair to take it out on someone who had tried to help.
examples.zh: 我说，冲一个曾经想帮忙的人「出气」不公平。

collocations: take it out on someone else
apologise for taking it out on someone
never take it out on someone

words.enDefinition: to draw a conclusion without enough evidence in a way that treats someone unfairly

examples.en: I did not want to make an unfair assumption about why he missed the meeting.
examples.zh: 我不想因为他没来开会就「对他妄下判断」。

examples.en: The tutor reminded us not to make an unfair assumption based on one quiet lesson.
examples.zh: 导师提醒我们，别因为有人一节课上没怎么说话就「对人妄下判断」。

collocations: avoid making an unfair assumption
make an unfair assumption about someone
apologise for making an unfair assumption

words.zhGloss: 把对方的付出当成理所当然
words.enDefinition: to fail to appreciate someone because you assume their help or presence will always be there
acceptedZhAnswers: 把对方的付出当成理所当然

examples.en: I realised I could take someone for granted simply by never thanking them for their help.
examples.zh: 我发现，一直不感谢别人帮忙，就是「把对方的付出当成理所当然」。

examples.en: It is easy to take someone for granted when they always organise the group meetings.
examples.zh: 别人总负责组织小组会议，很容易让人「把对方的付出当成理所当然」。

collocations: never take someone for granted
be careful not to take someone for granted
realise you take someone for granted

words.enDefinition: to unexpectedly leave someone without the support they need in a difficult situation

examples.en: I promised not to leave someone in the lurch again on the day of a presentation.
examples.zh: 我答应，下次演示当天不会再把「需要帮忙的人丢下不管」。

examples.en: Cancel early if you must, so you don't leave someone in the lurch at the last minute.
examples.zh: 非取消不可的话就早点说，别到了最后一刻「丢下需要帮忙的人不管」。

collocations: leave someone in the lurch at the last minute
refuse to leave someone in the lurch
apologise for leaving someone in the lurch

words.enDefinition: to fail to do what you had definitely said you would do

examples.en: I did not want to break a promise to help her move during the weekend.
examples.zh: 我答应周末帮她搬家，我不想「不守承诺」。

examples.en: It feels worse to break a promise when other people have planned around your help.
examples.zh: 别人已经按你会来帮忙做好计划时，「不守承诺」会更让人难受。

collocations: break a promise to someone
admit you broke a promise
apologise for breaking a promise

words.enDefinition: to start or agree to do something and then neglect to complete it

examples.en: It damages trust if you fail to follow through after volunteering to check the references.
examples.zh: 主动说要核对参考文献，却「没有把答应的事做完」，会损害信任。

examples.en: I did not want to fail to follow through after offering to contact the venue.
examples.zh: 我主动提出联系场地，不希望「到头来没把答应的事做完」。

collocations: sometimes fail to follow through
fail to follow through on a commitment
apologise for failing to follow through

words.zhGloss: 在该负责的事上掉链子
words.enDefinition: to make a mistake by failing to handle a responsibility you were expected to manage
acceptedZhAnswers: 在该负责的事上掉链子

examples.en: I knew I could not drop the ball again on sending the final reminder.
examples.zh: 我知道发最后一条提醒是我该做的，不能再「掉链子」了。

examples.en: If we drop the ball on the room booking, the group has nowhere to meet.
examples.zh: 要是我们在订房间这件事上「掉链子」，小组就没地方开会了。

collocations: drop the ball on a task
admit you dropped the ball
apologise for dropping the ball

words.enDefinition: to accidentally say something embarrassing, tactless or upsetting, chiefly in British English
acceptedEnVariants: put your foot in your mouth

examples.en: You can put your foot in it by asking about plans someone had to cancel.
examples.zh: 去问别人不得不取消的计划，有可能会「说了不该说的话」。

examples.en: I never meant to put my foot in it by mentioning the old rehearsal space.
examples.zh: 提起以前的排练场地时，我没想到会「说了不该说的话」。

collocations: really put your foot in it
accidentally put your foot in it
put your foot in it again

words.zhGloss: 承认自己从前的话说错了
words.enDefinition: to have to admit that an earlier statement, often a confident prediction, was wrong
acceptedZhAnswers: 承认自己从前的话说错了

examples.en: I had to eat my words after our new member finished the design in a day.
examples.zh: 新成员一天就做完了设计，我只好「承认自己之前的话说错了」。

examples.en: You'll have to eat your words if the small theatre sells out again this weekend.
examples.zh: 要是这个周末小剧场又售罄，你就得「承认自己从前的话说错了」。

collocations: have to eat your words
make someone eat their words
be forced to eat your words

words.enDefinition: to say you no longer stand by a statement you made earlier

examples.en: You can't fully take back what you said, but you can apologise for saying it.
examples.zh: 你不能真的「收回你说过的话」，但可以为说过那番话道歉。

examples.en: Are you willing to take back what you said about our volunteer coordinator yesterday morning?
examples.zh: 你愿意「收回你说过的话」吗，就是昨天上午你谈到我们志愿者协调员时那些话？

collocations: want to take back what you said
ask someone to take back what they said
wish you could take back what you said

words.zhGloss: 缓和或收回先前的言论
words.enDefinition: to soften, qualify or partially withdraw something you previously said
acceptedZhAnswers: 缓和或收回先前的言论

examples.en: The chair tried to walk back a remark about cancelling the student event that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午，主席试图「缓和先前的言论」，他说过要取消学生活动。

examples.en: It was difficult to walk back a remark that everyone had already quoted in the group chat.
examples.zh: 大家已经在群聊里引用过那句话，很难再「收回先前的言论」。

collocations: try to walk back a remark
publicly walk back a remark
walk back a remark made earlier

words.enDefinition: to provide accurate information after someone has formed the wrong idea about a situation

examples.en: I wanted to correct a false impression after my message sounded more critical than intended.
examples.zh: 我的消息听着比本意更像批评，我想「纠正错误印象」。

examples.en: We held a short meeting to correct a false impression about who approved the changes.
examples.zh: 我们开了个短会，「纠正关于谁批准了修改的错误印象」。

collocations: try to correct a false impression
correct a false impression about someone
write to correct a false impression

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge the people who deserve recognition for their contribution

examples.en: We should give credit where it's due and thank the volunteers who designed the display.
examples.zh: 我们应该「把功劳归给应得的人」，感谢设计展示台的志愿者。

examples.en: Our editor promised to give credit where it's due when the corrected article came out.
examples.zh: 编辑答应在更正后的报道刊出时「把功劳归给应得的人」。

collocations: always give credit where it's due
make sure to give credit where it's due
give credit where it's due in public

words.enDefinition: to do something for a person to compensate for disappointing or inconveniencing them

examples.en: I wanted to make it up to someone after forgetting their shift at the student café.
examples.zh: 我忘了帮人在学生咖啡厅顶班，想「做点事补偿对方」。

examples.en: You can make it up to someone by offering to cover a different shift next week.
examples.zh: 你可以主动提出下周替另一个班，「做点事补偿对方」。

collocations: want to make it up to someone
try to make it up to someone
offer to make it up to someone

words.enDefinition: to fix or reduce the harm caused by an action, mistake or dispute

examples.en: A follow-up meeting helped repair the damage after the group's public disagreement about the event.
examples.zh: 小组公开争论活动安排后，后续会议有助于「弥补造成的损害」。

examples.en: The editor contacted the affected volunteers to repair the damage from the inaccurate report.
examples.zh: 编辑联系了受影响的志愿者，「弥补不实报道造成的损害」。

collocations: try to repair the damage
help repair the damage
repair the damage caused by an error

words.zhGloss: 靠行动重新赢得某人的信任
words.enDefinition: to become trusted again by acting dependably over time after letting someone down
acceptedZhAnswers: 靠行动重新赢得某人的信任

examples.en: It takes time to earn back someone's trust when they were counting on you.
examples.zh: 对方原本指望你，这时候「重新赢得对方的信任」需要时间。

examples.en: You cannot earn back someone's trust just by sending a longer message the next day.
examples.zh: 仅仅第二天发条更长的消息，没法「重新赢得对方的信任」。

collocations: work to earn back someone's trust
try to earn back someone's trust
take time to earn back someone's trust

words.enDefinition: to do or finish what you promised, especially after taking the first step

examples.en: We wanted to follow through on a promise to find a quieter meeting room.
examples.zh: 我们承诺找个更安静的会议室，想「把承诺付诸行动」。

examples.en: It helps to set a deadline when you follow through on a promise to someone.
examples.zh: 要「把对别人的承诺付诸行动」时，定个截止时间会有帮助。

collocations: agree to follow through on a promise
manage to follow through on a promise
fail to follow through on a promise

words.enDefinition: to make a difficult or awkward situation calmer, sometimes without fully solving the problem

examples.en: She tried to smooth things over after two club members argued in the rehearsal room.
examples.zh: 两名社员在排练室吵了起来，她试着「缓和紧张局面」。

examples.en: A quick explanation helped smooth things over before everyone sat down for the next session.
examples.zh: 大家坐下来开始下一场前，简短的解释有助于「缓和尴尬局面」。

collocations: try to smooth things over
help smooth things over
smooth things over with someone

words.enDefinition: to make an offer or gesture showing that you want to end a disagreement

examples.en: Our group chose to extend an olive branch by inviting both organisers to the planning meeting.
examples.zh: 我们小组邀请两名组织者都来开筹备会，以此「主动释放和解信号」。

examples.en: The chair tried to extend an olive branch after the debate over using the room.
examples.zh: 两方就是否使用房间争执后，主席试图「主动释放和解信号」。

collocations: extend an olive branch to someone
try to extend an olive branch
choose to extend an olive branch

words.enDefinition: to start behaving in a better or more responsible way than before

examples.en: He promised to turn over a new leaf after missing three meetings in a row.
examples.zh: 他连续缺席三次会议后，答应「改过并重新做起」。

examples.en: I wanted to turn over a new leaf and actually reply to plans on time.
examples.zh: 我想「改过并重新做起」，以后发来安排时真的按时回应。

collocations: decide to turn over a new leaf
promise to turn over a new leaf
try to turn over a new leaf

words.enDefinition: to start again while agreeing not to count earlier mistakes against someone

examples.en: We agreed to wipe the slate clean before choosing roles for the new project.
examples.zh: 选新项目的分工前，我们同意「把过往清零，从头来过」。

examples.en: The committee wanted to wipe the slate clean after the new members heard both sides.
examples.zh: 新会员听过双方说法后，委员会希望「把过往清零，从头来过」。

collocations: agree to wipe the slate clean
want to wipe the slate clean
try to wipe the slate clean

words.enDefinition: to stop letting a past disagreement or unpleasant event affect how we deal with each other

examples.en: We decided to put it behind us after discussing why the weekend plans fell apart.
examples.zh: 我们谈过周末计划为什么没成之后，决定「把这件事翻篇」。

examples.en: I'd like to put it behind us before we start working on the final report.
examples.zh: 开始一起做最终报告前，我想「把这件事翻篇」。

collocations: decide to put it behind us
try to put it behind us
ready to put it behind us

words.enDefinition: to forgive someone and agree not to keep bringing up what they did

examples.en: I was willing to discuss it, but I wasn't ready to forgive and forget.
examples.zh: 我愿意谈这件事，但还没准备好「原谅并放下旧事」。

examples.en: They eventually chose to forgive and forget after months of avoiding each other on campus.
examples.zh: 他们在校园里互相躲了几个月，最后选择「原谅并放下旧事」。

collocations: be ready to forgive and forget
choose to forgive and forget
decide to forgive and forget

words.enDefinition: to keep feeling angry with a person because of something they did in the past

examples.en: I did not want to hold a grudge over one mistake in our first meeting.
examples.zh: 我不想因为第一次开会的一次失误就「记恨」。

examples.en: It is easy to hold a grudge when nobody ever talks about what went wrong.
examples.zh: 大家始终没谈出了什么差错，就很容易让人「记恨」。

collocations: hold a grudge against someone
refuse to hold a grudge
hold a grudge for years

words.enDefinition: to stop carrying anger or bitterness about unfair treatment in the past

examples.en: It took me a while to let go of resentment after being left out of decisions.
examples.zh: 之前做决定没算上我，我过了好一阵子才「放下积怨」。

examples.en: Our conversation helped me let go of resentment about how the project had ended.
examples.zh: 那次谈话让我能「放下积怨」，不再纠结项目是怎么收场的。

collocations: find it hard to let go of resentment
learn to let go of resentment
help someone let go of resentment

words.enDefinition: a friendly expression showing or asking that there be no lasting anger after a disagreement

examples.en: No hard feelings. I know the room mix-up was hard for everyone to sort out.
examples.zh: 「我没往心里去」。我知道房间弄混了，大家都不好处理。

examples.en: We agreed there were no hard feelings after talking about how the schedule had changed.
examples.zh: 我们谈过时间表怎么改的，确认「彼此都没往心里去」。

collocations: there are no hard feelings
hope there are no hard feelings
say no hard feelings

words.enDefinition: to allow a person to try again after a previous mistake or failure

examples.en: It's easier to give someone another chance when they say what they will actually change.
examples.zh: 别人说清楚自己具体会改什么时，更容易「再给对方一次机会」。

examples.en: It is sometimes fair to give someone another chance after a single honest mistake.
examples.zh: 有时别人只犯了一次无心的错，「再给对方一次机会」才公平。

collocations: decide to give someone another chance
be willing to give someone another chance
choose to give someone another chance

words.enDefinition: acknowledges someone's apology in a positive way without necessarily saying everything is resolved

examples.en: I appreciate the apology, and I'm glad we could talk before seeing the others.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你向我道歉」，也很高兴我们能在见其他人之前谈一谈。

examples.en: I appreciate the apology, though I would still like to discuss what changes next time.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你向我道歉」，不过我还是想谈谈下次要做哪些调整。

collocations: say I appreciate the apology
I appreciate the apology and the explanation
I appreciate the apology you offered

words.enDefinition: expresses gratitude that someone has acknowledged something they did wrong

examples.en: Thank you for owning up before we sent the incorrect sign-up list to the organisers.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你坦白承认」，幸好我们还没把有误的报名名单发给组织者。

examples.en: Thank you for owning up. Now we can work out who needs the corrected information.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你坦白承认」。现在可以弄清哪些人需要收到更正后的信息。

collocations: say thank you for owning up
thank you for owning up to it
thank you for owning up so quickly

words.enDefinition: asks for time to process a difficult event or apology before responding or moving on

examples.en: I'll need some time before I am ready to talk about yesterday's disagreement again.
examples.zh: 「我需要一点时间」，之后才能再谈昨天的争执。

examples.en: I'll need some time to think about what you said before we meet on Friday.
examples.zh: 「我需要一点时间」想想你说的话，周五见面时再谈。

collocations: I'll need some time to think
I'll need some time before we talk
I'll need some time to get used to it

words.enDefinition: asks for temporary distance or reduced contact, often after an upsetting interaction

examples.en: I need some space tonight, so let's talk about what happened after class tomorrow.
examples.zh: 今晚「我需要一点独处空间」，发生的事明天下课后再谈吧。

examples.en: I need some space before I can talk calmly about how the meeting went.
examples.zh: 「我需要一点独处空间」，之后才能平静地聊那场会议。

collocations: I need some space for a while
I need some space right now
say I need some space

words.enDefinition: asks whether tension between two people has eased after a disagreement or apology

examples.en: After we discussed the missed rehearsal, I asked my partner, Are we okay now?
examples.zh: 我们谈过错过排练的事后，我问搭档：「我们现在和好了吗」？

examples.en: Are we okay now, or would you rather give it another day before we talk?
examples.zh: 「我们现在和好了吗」，还是你想再等一天才谈？

collocations: are we okay now after talking it through
are we okay now or do you need more time
are we okay now about what happened

words.enDefinition: often light-heartedly says that a mistake has been forgiven and is no longer an issue

examples.en: All is forgiven, my friend said when I showed up with the missing snacks.
examples.zh: 我带着之前忘拿的零食出现时，朋友说：「过去的错就不计较了」。

examples.en: We both laughed when the organiser said all is forgiven and handed me the new schedule.
examples.zh: 组织者说「过去的错就不计较了」，把新时间表递给我，我们俩都笑了。

collocations: say all is forgiven
all is forgiven now
all is forgiven this time

words.enDefinition: reassures someone that you do not think an apology is necessary

examples.en: No need to apologize, we still had enough chairs before the other students arrived.
examples.zh: 「不用道歉」，其他同学到之前，椅子还是够的。

examples.en: No need to apologize for asking twice because the instructions were hard to hear.
examples.zh: 刚才说明没听清，多问一遍也「不用道歉」。

collocations: say no need to apologize
there is no need to apologize
no need to apologize for asking

words.expression: I won't hold it against you
words.lemma: i won't hold it against you
words.enDefinition: reassures someone that a past mistake will not affect how you judge or treat them
acceptedEnVariants: I won't hold it against you

examples.en: I won't hold it against you if you forgot once during your first week here.
examples.zh: 你才来第一周，如果就忘了这一次，「我不会因此怪你」。

examples.en: I won't hold it against you, but please tell me sooner if it happens again.
examples.zh: 「我不会因此怪你」，不过下次再发生，早点告诉我。

collocations: say I won't hold it against you
I won't hold it against you this time
explain I won't hold it against you

words.enDefinition: tells someone not to be overly harsh or ashamed about a mistake

examples.en: Don't beat yourself up over one missed deadline in an otherwise difficult first term.
examples.zh: 第一学期本来就不容易，漏了一个截止日期，「别太责怪自己」。

examples.en: Don't beat yourself up, we can still change the date before people reserve their tickets.
examples.zh: 「别太责怪自己」，大家还没订票，我们还能改日期。

collocations: don't beat yourself up about it
don't beat yourself up over a mistake
remember not to beat yourself up

words.expression: I'll be more careful next time
words.lemma: i'll be more careful next time
words.enDefinition: promises to pay closer attention in a similar situation in the future
acceptedEnVariants: I'll be more careful next time

examples.en: I'll be more careful next time when I send the mailing list to the printer.
examples.zh: 下次把邮寄名单交给印刷方时，「我会更小心」。

examples.en: I'll be more careful next time and double-check the room before I send the reminder.
examples.zh: 「下次我会更小心」，发提醒前我会再核对一遍房间。

collocations: say I'll be more careful next time
I'll be more careful next time we meet
promise I'll be more careful next time

words.enDefinition: promises or assures someone that a mistake or problem will not be repeated

examples.en: I've corrected the invitation list, and it won't happen again at the next meeting.
examples.zh: 我已更正邀请名单，下次开会「不会再发生这种事了」。

examples.en: It won't happen again now that both of us will check the room booking.
examples.zh: 现在我们两个人都会核对房间预约，「不会再发生这种事了」。

collocations: promise it won't happen again
say it won't happen again
make sure it won't happen again

words.enDefinition: to treat a person fairly or do what they deserve, especially when you owe them something

examples.en: I wanted to do right by someone who had missed a shift to help us.
examples.zh: 有人为了帮我们错过一班工作，我想「好好对待那个人」。

examples.en: A fair division of the proceeds lets us do right by someone who contributed their time.
examples.zh: 公平分配所得，能「公正对待为此付出时间的人」。

collocations: try to do right by someone
want to do right by someone
make an effort to do right by someone

words.enDefinition: to make a firm promise to improve one's future behaviour or performance

examples.en: I wanted to commit to doing better by including new volunteers in our planning discussions.
examples.zh: 我想「承诺今后改进」，让新志愿者也能参与我们的筹备讨论。

examples.en: The team decided to commit to doing better instead of treating the complaint as resolved.
examples.zh: 团队决定「承诺今后改进」，不把收到投诉就算作问题解决。

collocations: choose to commit to doing better
publicly commit to doing better
be ready to commit to doing better

words.zhGloss: 行动比言语更有说服力
words.enDefinition: a proverb meaning that behaviour reveals commitment more clearly than promises do
acceptedZhAnswers: 行动比言语更有说服力

examples.en: Actions speak louder than words, so I waited to see whether he kept his promise.
examples.zh: 「行动比言语更有说服力」，所以我等着看他是否守诺。

examples.en: Our tutor reminded us that actions speak louder than words when a team is rebuilding trust.
examples.zh: 导师提醒我们，团队重新建立信任时，「行动比言语更有说服力」。

collocations: remember that actions speak louder than words
prove that actions speak louder than words
as they say, actions speak louder than words

words.enDefinition: to show through words or actions that you regret doing something wrong

examples.en: She wanted to show remorse for leaving the first volunteer out of the discussion.
examples.zh: 她没有让第一位志愿者参与讨论，想为此「表现出悔意」。

examples.en: His words did not show remorse until he spoke about the people the decision affected.
examples.zh: 直到他说起受决定影响的人，他的话里才「表现出悔意」。

collocations: show remorse for your actions
fail to show remorse
show genuine remorse

words.enDefinition: to act honestly and sincerely, without trying to deceive or take unfair advantage

examples.en: Both organisers agreed to act in good faith while checking the facts about the booking.
examples.zh: 两名组织者同意，在核对预订的实际情况时「本着诚意行事」。

examples.en: I think she did act in good faith when she passed along the wrong date.
examples.zh: 虽然她传错了日期，但我认为她的确是「本着诚意行事」。

collocations: agree to act in good faith
believe both sides act in good faith
be expected to act in good faith

words.expression: I'm sorry you had to deal with that
words.lemma: i'm sorry you had to deal with that
words.zhGloss: 你还得应付那件事，真不好受
words.enDefinition: expresses sympathy or regret that someone had to handle an unpleasant situation
acceptedZhAnswers: 你还得应付那件事，真不好受
acceptedEnVariants: I'm sorry you had to deal with that

examples.en: I'm sorry you had to deal with that while I was away at the conference.
examples.zh: 我离开去参加会议时，「你还得应付那件事，真不好受」。

examples.en: I'm sorry you had to deal with that on top of finishing your own project.
examples.zh: 你还得完成自己的项目，又得「应付那件事，真不好受」。

collocations: I'm sorry you had to deal with that alone
I'm sorry you had to deal with that on your first day
I'm really sorry you had to deal with that

words.expression: put someone in a difficult position
words.lemma: put someone in a difficult position
words.enDefinition: to put someone in circumstances where their possible choices are awkward or difficult
acceptedEnVariants: put someone in a difficult position

examples.en: I did not want to put someone in a difficult position by asking them to choose sides.
examples.zh: 我不想逼人选边站，「让对方为难」。

examples.en: It can put someone in a difficult position to discuss their mistake in front of others.
examples.zh: 当着大家的面谈一个人的过错，可能会「让那个人为难」。

collocations: unintentionally put someone in a difficult position
avoid putting someone in a difficult position
apologise for putting someone in a difficult position

words.enDefinition: to cause tension or discomfort between people who are interacting

examples.en: I worried that bringing up the old email would make things awkward before the meeting.
examples.zh: 我怕开会前提起那封旧邮件会「让场面变得尴尬」。

examples.en: You can apologise without going into details that might make things awkward for the group.
examples.zh: 你可以道歉，细节就不用说了，免得「让小组里的场面变得尴尬」。

collocations: try not to make things awkward
worry about making things awkward
make things awkward for someone

words.enDefinition: to mention a mistake with little detail in a way that makes it seem unimportant

examples.en: I did not want to gloss over a mistake that affected the whole volunteer team.
examples.zh: 这个错影响了整个志愿者团队，我不想「轻描淡写地带过」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to explain what happened rather than gloss over a mistake in the report.
examples.zh: 导师请我们说明发生了什么，别在报告里「轻描淡写地带过错误」。

collocations: try to gloss over a mistake
refuse to gloss over a mistake
apologise without trying to gloss over a mistake

words.enDefinition: lasting hostility or bitterness between people who have had a disagreement

examples.en: There was still bad blood between the two groups when they shared the rehearsal hall.
examples.zh: 两个小组共用排练厅时，彼此之间仍有「旧怨」。

examples.en: We wanted to resolve the booking issue before it created bad blood among the volunteers.
examples.zh: 我们想处理好预约问题，免得志愿者之间结下「怨隙」。

collocations: there is bad blood between them
create bad blood
leave bad blood

words.enDefinition: to resolve an issue so people can stop discussing or worrying about it

examples.en: We hoped that speaking directly to the organisers would finally put the matter to rest.
examples.zh: 我们希望直接跟组织者谈，最终能「让这件事有个了结」。

examples.en: The corrected meeting minutes helped put the matter to rest before the next committee meeting.
examples.zh: 更正后的会议纪要有助于在下次委员会会议前「让这件事有个了结」。

collocations: finally put the matter to rest
help put the matter to rest
try to put the matter to rest

words.enDefinition: a short direct response acknowledging that you accept what a person has said in apology

examples.en: Apology accepted, my teammate said after I returned the equipment to the correct cupboard.
examples.zh: 我把器材放回正确的柜子后，队友说：「我接受道歉」。

examples.en: She said apology accepted, and we agreed to talk about the schedule the next morning.
examples.zh: 她说「我接受道歉」，我们约好第二天早上再谈时间表。

collocations: apology accepted, thanks for explaining
apology accepted, let's leave it there
okay, apology accepted

words.enDefinition: to ask someone not to keep feeling anger or blame for something wrong you did

examples.en: I wanted to ask for forgiveness after repeating something my friend had told me privately.
examples.zh: 我把朋友私下告诉我的事说了出去，想「请求原谅」。

examples.en: He chose to ask for forgiveness once the other volunteers had heard his full explanation.
examples.zh: 其他志愿者听完他的解释后，他选择「请求原谅」。

collocations: choose to ask for forgiveness
ask for forgiveness directly
be ready to ask for forgiveness

words.enDefinition: a direct request to be forgiven for something the speaker did

examples.en: Please forgive me for sharing your draft without asking whether it was ready to circulate.
examples.zh: 我没问你的草稿能不能传就分享出去了，「请原谅我」。

examples.en: Please forgive me for being careless with something you trusted me to look after.
examples.zh: 你信任我，托我保管的东西我没照看好，「请原谅我」。

collocations: please forgive me for the mistake
please forgive me if I upset you
say please forgive me

words.enDefinition: an informal way to say that an apology alone does not address the harm or problem

examples.en: Sorry doesn't cut it if we still have to redo the whole booking ourselves.
examples.zh: 如果还是得我们自己把整个预约重办一遍，那「光道歉还不够」。

examples.en: He said sorry doesn't cut it after we missed the same deadline a second time.
examples.zh: 我们第二次错过同一个截止日期后，他说「光道歉还不够」。

collocations: say sorry doesn't cut it
feel that sorry doesn't cut it
sorry doesn't cut it anymore

words.enDefinition: describes an effort that is insufficient and arrives after it could have made a difference

examples.en: The extra rehearsal was too little too late after most of the performers had left.
examples.zh: 大部分演员都离开后才补排一场，「补救太少，也来得太晚」。

examples.en: For the volunteers who had lost their places, that apology was too little too late.
examples.zh: 对失去名额的志愿者来说，那份道歉「补救太少，也来得太晚」。

collocations: be too little too late
feel like too little too late
describe an offer as too little too late

words.expression: you don't have to forgive me
words.lemma: you don't have to forgive me
words.enDefinition: acknowledges that the other person is under no obligation to forgive after an apology
acceptedEnVariants: you don't have to forgive me

examples.en: You don't have to forgive me, but I wanted you to hear me acknowledge the mistake.
examples.zh: 「你不必原谅我」，但我想让你亲耳听到我承认过错。

examples.en: You don't have to forgive me right now, and I won't bring it up again tonight.
examples.zh: 现在「你不必原谅我」，今晚我也不会再提这事。

collocations: you don't have to forgive me today
you don't have to forgive me right away
say you don't have to forgive me

words.enDefinition: describes taking responsibility or explaining what happened without trying to avoid blame

examples.en: She explained why the tickets were missing without making excuses for how she handled them.
examples.zh: 她解释了票为什么不见了，「没有为自己的处理方式找借口」。

examples.en: I wanted to apologise without making excuses for forgetting the equipment we needed that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午要用的器材我忘了带，我想道歉，「不为自己找借口」。

collocations: apologise without making excuses
take responsibility without making excuses
explain without making excuses

words.enDefinition: admits that one's behaviour was inappropriate, disrespectful or went beyond what was acceptable

examples.en: I was out of line when I criticised your work in front of the whole group.
examples.zh: 我当着整个小组的面批评你的作品，「我那样做过分了」。

examples.en: I was out of line, and you were right to tell me to stop.
examples.zh: 「我那样做过分了」，你让我停下来是对的。

collocations: admit I was out of line
say I was out of line
I was out of line yesterday

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that the other person deserves to know why something happened or what you did

examples.en: I owe you an explanation for leaving the meeting before your part of the discussion.
examples.zh: 你的讨论环节还没到我就先走了，「我应该给你一个解释」。

examples.en: I owe you an explanation about why your name was missing from the final schedule.
examples.zh: 最终的时间表上为什么没你的名字，「我应该给你一个解释」。

collocations: I owe you an explanation for leaving
I owe you an explanation about the change
say I owe you an explanation

words.enDefinition: says that you would consider another person's reaction understandable in the circumstances

examples.en: I wouldn't blame you if you decided not to volunteer with us again next term.
examples.zh: 如果你决定下学期不再跟我们做志愿工作，「我不会怪你」。

examples.en: I wouldn't blame you for being annoyed after waiting outside the locked room with everyone.
examples.zh: 你和大家一起在上锁的房间外等了半天，就算生气，「我也不会怪你」。

collocations: I wouldn't blame you for feeling that way
I wouldn't blame you for leaving
I wouldn't blame you if you said no

words.enDefinition: admits that you did not give enough attention to what someone said or advised

examples.en: I should have listened when you warned me the last bus left before eleven.
examples.zh: 你提醒我末班车十一点前就开走，「我当初应该认真听」。

examples.en: I should have listened instead of deciding I knew what the group wanted to do.
examples.zh: 「我当初应该认真听」，不该自认知道大家想怎么做。

collocations: I should have listened to you
I should have listened more carefully
admit I should have listened

words.enDefinition: a comment that causes someone emotional pain or distress

examples.en: His hurtful remark was about my accent, and I remembered it for a long time.
examples.zh: 他那句「伤人的话」是针对我的口音，我记了很久。

examples.en: I asked her to withdraw the hurtful remark before we continued discussing the project.
examples.zh: 项目讨论继续之前，我请她收回那句「伤人的话」。

collocations: make a hurtful remark
apologise for a hurtful remark
take back a hurtful remark

words.enDefinition: acknowledges that one's reaction was more intense than the situation called for

examples.en: I overreacted when you told me the meeting had moved to the smaller room.
examples.zh: 你告诉我会议改到较小的房间时，「我反应过头了」。

examples.en: I overreacted, and I should have waited to hear what the organiser had said.
examples.zh: 「我反应过头了」，我应该先听听组织者是怎么说的。

collocations: admit I overreacted
say I overreacted
I overreacted a little

words.expression: give someone the benefit of the doubt
words.lemma: give someone the benefit of the doubt
words.enDefinition: to assume someone is honest or meant well when you are unsure what happened
acceptedEnVariants: give someone the benefit of the doubt

examples.en: I tried to give someone the benefit of the doubt rather than repeating a rumour.
examples.zh: 事还没弄清楚，我试着「先相信对方」，没有转述传闻。

examples.en: It is easier to give someone the benefit of the doubt after hearing their explanation.
examples.zh: 听过对方的解释后，更容易「在事情没弄清前先相信对方」。

collocations: choose to give someone the benefit of the doubt
be willing to give someone the benefit of the doubt
ask others to give someone the benefit of the doubt

words.enDefinition: to do what you told another person you would do

examples.en: You can keep your word by sending the corrected timetable before noon as you promised.
examples.zh: 按约定在中午前发出更正后的时间表，就能「说到做到」。

examples.en: In a group project, you have to keep your word if you want people to trust you.
examples.zh: 做小组项目时，如果想让别人信任你，就得「说到做到」。

collocations: always keep your word
promise to keep your word
learn to keep your word

words.enDefinition: an apology communicated in writing, such as in a formal letter, email or statement

examples.en: The volunteers received a written apology from the committee after the incident was reviewed.
examples.zh: 复核那件事后，志愿者收到了委员会的「书面道歉」。

examples.en: A written apology reached everyone who had received the incorrect notice about the closure.
examples.zh: 收到错误闭馆通知的每个人都拿到了「书面道歉」。

collocations: send a written apology
receive a written apology
request a written apology

words.zhGloss: 对造成的困扰表示遗憾
words.enDefinition: a formal expression of regret for any distress a person or organisation may have caused
acceptedZhAnswers: 对造成的困扰表示遗憾

examples.en: In our response, we said we regret any distress caused by the mistaken announcement.
examples.zh: 我们在回应中说：「对错误通知造成的困扰表示遗憾」。

examples.en: The organisers wrote that they regret any distress caused to people who were named.
examples.zh: 组织者写道，他们「对给被点名的人造成的困扰表示遗憾」。

collocations: regret any distress caused
regret any distress this caused
state that you regret any distress

words.enDefinition: a feeling of guilt about something you believe you did wrong

examples.en: I had a guilty conscience after taking credit for an idea my partner came up with.
examples.zh: 搭档想出的点子被我当成自己的功劳，此后我一直「良心不安」。

examples.en: My guilty conscience made it harder to enjoy the celebration at the end of term.
examples.zh: 因为「良心不安」，我没法尽情享受学期末的庆祝活动。

collocations: have a guilty conscience
ease a guilty conscience
act out of a guilty conscience

words.expression: get off on the wrong foot
words.lemma: get off on the wrong foot
words.zhGloss: 一开头就相处得不太顺
words.enDefinition: to begin a relationship or shared activity in an awkward or unfriendly way
acceptedZhAnswers: 一开头就相处得不太顺
acceptedEnVariants: get off on the wrong foot

examples.en: It's easy to get off on the wrong foot when nobody explains how roles were assigned.
examples.zh: 没人解释角色是怎么分配的，就很容易「一开头就相处得不太顺」。

examples.en: We did get off on the wrong foot, but things improved by the second meeting.
examples.zh: 我们的确是「一开头就相处得不太顺」，到第二次会议时情况好转了。

collocations: get off on the wrong foot with someone
seem to get off on the wrong foot
avoid getting off on the wrong foot
